shrub.name: Frailejon
shrub.source: Espeletia grandiflora, Colombian Eastern Cordillera paramo 2700-4200 m, woolly stem-rosette 0.5-3 m with yellow daisies

traits.native_range: Espeletia grandiflora, Colombian Eastern Cordillera paramo 2700-4200 m, woolly stem-rosette 0
traits.note: leaf/trunk/petiole derived from the plant's shape class; per-species detail where the entry carries it (aroids, cannabis)

shrub.silhouette: woolly rosette atop skirt of dead leaves

growth.juvenile_note: Seedlings are tiny flat rosettes of woolly, silver-green, strap-shaped leaves on bare ground or moss (~85% die in dry spells). For about 4-5 years a stemless ground rosette widens to 25-30 cm; then the stem begins to rise ~7-8 cm a year, clothed in a skirt of dead leaves, and the plant can first flower at ~20 cm of stem.
growth.source: Fagua & Gonzalez 2007 Plant Biology (E. grandiflora: stem growth 7.6 cm/yr, plants >=2 m ~40-45 yr old, first flowering at ~21 cm stem, seedling mortality ~85% in dry season); Exotica Esoterica frailejon cultivation notes (stemless for 4+ yr, 25-30 cm rosette in <2 yr, ~90% germination within 3 months).

fruiting.source: Fagua & Gonzalez 2007 Plant Biology (flowering peak Oct-Nov, 30-96 days per plant; inflorescence stalks ~85 cm; heads 5.0-6.2 cm, ~86 per plant; Bombus the main pollinators plus hummingbirds, flies, beetles, nocturnal moths; seeds shed Sep-May). Achene size, crop and rot estimated.

traits.native_range: Puya clava-herculis, Ecuadorian paramo 3300-4400 m, spiny terrestrial bromeliad rosette 1-2
traits.leaf_shape: stiff spined sword leaves in a rosette
traits.trunk: none or a short woody stem; tall flower spike
traits.note: leaf/trunk/petiole derived from the plant's shape class; per-species detail where the entry carries it (aroids, cannabis)

shrub.silhouette: spiky grey rosette with club flower spike

growth.juvenile_note: A tiny grass-like tuft among paramo bunchgrass that slowly becomes a stemless rosette of stiff, narrow, channelled grey-green leaves with small hooked spines along the edges and silvery scales beneath. It widens for many years; finally one thick, club-shaped spike densely wrapped in white-buff wool rises from the centre, flowers, and the rosette dies.
growth.source: Kew POWO (perennial of the paramo, SW Colombia to Ecuador); Wikipedia Puya (many species monocarpic); Miller 1986 Oecologia (woolly inflorescences of Ecuadorian paramo Puya keep flowers warmer at night; from knowledge); ages and rates estimated from Puya raimondii and other paramo giant rosettes

fruiting.source: Estimated from paramo Puya (P. hamata, P. raimondii): tubular greenish flowers half hidden in the woolly spike, visited by hummingbirds (e.g. Ecuadorian hillstar) and bumblebees; individuals flower at any time of year; capsules split on the dead standing spike, releasing small winged seeds

shrub.name: Tall frailejon
shrub.origin: Andes of Ecuador and S Colombia
shrub.source: Espeletia pycnophylla, Ecuador/S Colombia paramo (El Angel), columnar stem-rosette to 6 m, dense stands

traits.native_range: Espeletia pycnophylla, Ecuador/S Colombia paramo (El Angel), columnar stem-rosette to 6 m, dense stands
traits.note: leaf/trunk/petiole derived from the plant's shape class; per-species detail where the entry carries it (aroids, cannabis)

shrub.silhouette: tall column of dead leaves, woolly rosette on top

growth.juvenile_note: Like other frailejones: a flat, silvery-woolly rosette of narrow leaves at ground level for several years, then a stem rises very slowly (a few cm a year), wrapped in a thick skirt of dead, hanging grey leaves under a dense crown rosette of felted silver-green leaves; old plants are shaggy columns 2-6 m tall.
growth.source: Estimated from Espeletia: Useful Tropical Plants (E. pycnophylla to ~4 m, slow); Cumbal (Narino) transplant study in Ingeniare (young plants +0.7-0.95 cm per 6 months); Fagua & Gonzalez 2007 (E. grandiflora 7.6 cm/yr); Flora 2018 long-term growth of Coespeletia and E. schultzii (~1.1-1.3 cm/yr).

fruiting.source: Estimated from E. grandiflora (Fagua & Gonzalez 2007 Plant Biology: yellow heads ~5-6 cm on long stalks, bumblebee/hummingbird/fly/beetle pollination, seed shed over months) and frailejon growers' notes (a stalk flowers ~2 months).

ground.name: Bog moss
ground.source: Sphagnum magellanicum, Andean paramo bogs and southern S America, red peat moss carpets

traits.native_range: Sphagnum magellanicum, Andean paramo bogs and southern S America, red peat moss carpets
traits.note: leaf/trunk/petiole derived from the plant's shape class; per-species detail where the entry carries it (aroids, cannabis)

growth.juvenile_note: A spore germinates into a tiny flat green plate that buds leafy shoots. The young colony is a soft cushion of fat, blunt, wine-red to purplish capitula (greener in shade) with swollen, spoon-shaped leaves, growing 1-3 cm taller a year in wet lawns and spreading into a spongy carpet.
growth.source: Springer Wetl. Ecol. Manag. 2019 (Chiloe, Chile: ~5.6 mm growth in 3 months, ~2 cm/yr); Diaz et al. 2012 Rev. Chil. Hist. Nat. (growth higher in lawns than hummocks); Bengtsson et al. 2016 (magellanicum-group 1-7 mm/yr in Sweden); shading aids regeneration (Can. J. Bot. 2025)

growth.juvenile_note: Seedlings are tiny rosettes of narrow, stiff, grey-green leaves; each keeps branching into more tight rosettes packed side by side, building a hard, convex, green cushion as firm as a pillow. Old cushions fuse into mounds and hummocks in wet paramo bogs, with small brownish flower spikes barely raised above the surface.
growth.source: Estimated from Andean paramo cushion-bog ecology (Plantago rigida and Distichia cushions: slow radial growth of millimetres to a few cm a year, cushions persisting for decades to centuries) and Plantago seed biology

ground.silhouette: woolly silver rosette with blue spike

growth.juvenile_note: Seedlings show two thick cotyledons, then small palmate leaves densely clothed in silky silver hairs. For years the plant builds a dense, silvery-woolly rosette of palmately divided leaves hugging the paramo ground, then sends up a single thick, woolly, fox-tail spike packed with blue-violet pea flowers, sets seed and dies.
growth.source: Wikipedia (Lupinus alopecuroides: 2,700-4,500 m on ten isolated peaks in Colombia and Ecuador); giant-rosette, flower-once (monocarpic) life history and timings estimated from paramo rosette lupines such as L. weberbaueri - treat as uncertain.
